correctness.rationale: For finite nonempty \(F\), choose \(q\notin F-F\) and a short interval whose translates by the finite set \((-F)\cup(q-F)\) are disjoint. Indicator functions of that interval and its \(q\)-translate have disjoint finite orbit-coordinate supports pointwise, which gives the exact \(\ell_1^2\) norm identity for every scalar pair. The failures of strict convexity and Gâteaux smoothness are immediate and wMLUR implies strict convexity. The tail estimate follows from \(\sqrt{A+B}-\sqrt A\le\sqrt B\), \(\ell_2\le\ell_1\), Tonelli, and invariance of Lebesgue measure. The full-source Theorems 3.4--3.5 verify the infinite-coordinate ergodic endpoint.

originality.rationale: The defining paper explicitly proves the full infinite-coordinate equivalence between ergodicity, strict convexity, smoothness, and absence of isometric \(\ell_1^2\), and it explicitly uses finite symmetric truncations with the same uniform tail estimate. However, full-paper inspection through the further-remarks section does not state that every finite-support truncation contains \(\ell_1^2\) even when the underlying transformation is ergodic. That statement lies outside Theorem 3.4 because its norm assumes every orbit weight is positive. The new disjoint-translate construction therefore gives a genuine finite-stage obstruction rather than restating the source's approximation estimate.

value.rationale: The source's main construction solves a geometric compatibility problem by using the full orbit. Showing that every finite approximation loses all of the relevant rotundity/smoothness while converging uniformly isolates an exact infinite-coordinate phenomenon and gives a sharp warning about finite-horizon approximations of this natural norm.

final_claim: For the irrational-rotation orbit norm of Dantas--Kaasik--Perreau, every nonempty finite orbit-window truncation contains an isometric \(\ell_1^2\), hence is neither strictly convex, Gâteaux smooth, nor wMLUR, although any increasing finite exhaustion converges uniformly to the full ergodic wMLUR/smooth norm on the \(L_1\)-unit ball at the tail rate \(\sum_{k\notin F}\sqrt{a_k}\).
limitations: The exact finite-window obstruction is proved for irrational rotation on the circle, not every ergodic transformation.
No claim is made about the Daugavet property of the truncated norms.
The uniform truncation estimate itself is already present in the defining source; originality is confined to the exact finite-stage geometry and its juxtaposition with that approximation.
